concept_use.Diametrical form of circle: The circle with AB as diameter, (x+1)(x-5)+(y-3)(y+5)=0, centre (2,-1), radius 5, carries all points with angle APB = pi/2.
concept_use.Basic geometry about circle: Basic geometry: angle in a semicircle is a right angle, points inside see AB at an obtuse angle, and a line meeting but not entering a circle is a tangent (distance from centre = radius).

english: Let $A=(-1,3)$ and $B=(5,-5)$. Let $S$ be the set of all real numbers $k$ for which the line $2x-y=k$ contains a point $P$ with $\angle APB=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ but contains no point $Q$ with $\angle AQB>\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Then the product of all the elements of $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A=(-1,3)$ तथा $B=(5,-5)$ हैं। माना $S$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $k$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए रेखा $2x-y=k$ पर एक बिन्दु $P$ ऐसा है कि $\angle APB=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ है, परन्तु रेखा पर कोई बिन्दु $Q$ ऐसा नहीं है कि $\angle AQB>\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ हो। तब $S$ के सभी अवयवों का गुणनफल ______ है।
solution: $\angle APB=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\iff P$ is on the circle with diameter $AB$ ($P\neq A,B$); $\angle AQB>\dfrac{\pi}{2}\iff Q$ is inside it (not on segment $AB$)
So the line must meet the circle but not enter it: it is a tangent (the tangents at $A$, $B$ have slope $\dfrac{3}{4}\neq2$, so the point of contact is not $A$ or $B$)
solution_full: Angle in a semicircle: $\angle APB=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ exactly when $P$ lies on the circle with $AB$ as diameter and $P\neq A,B$.
A point $Q$ inside this circle and not on the segment $AB$ sees $AB$ under an obtuse angle; a point outside sees it under an acute angle.

If the line cut the circle at two points, the open chord between them would contain points $Q$ inside the circle with $\angle AQB>\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ (only finitely many of them can lie on $AB$). So the line must be a tangent.

The tangent must touch at a point other than $A$ and $B$. The tangents at $A$ and $B$ are perpendicular to $AB$ (slope $-\dfrac{4}{3}$), so they have slope $\dfrac{3}{4}$, while $2x-y=k$ has slope $2$. Hence every tangent of slope $2$ touches at an admissible point $P$.
Tangency: distance of $(2,-1)$ from $2x-y-k=0$ equals $5$: $\dfrac{|5-k|}{\sqrt{5}}=5$, so $(k-5)^{2}=125$, $k=5\pm5\sqrt{5}$.
originality_note: New: a line condition written purely in terms of angles (a right angle is attained but no obtuse angle) that has to be decoded, through the angle-in-a-semicircle fact and its strict version, into tangency to the circle on AB as diameter (way 5). Closest known: points P on a line with angle APB = 90 degrees, i.e. intersections with the diametric circle. Different because: the inequality excludes secants, so the student must reach tangency from the geometry rather than from a count of roots.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, curve and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, and the Hindi mirrors the English. First draft asked for 'exactly one point P with angle APB = pi/2'; lines through A or B (k = -5, 15) also had exactly one such point, so the condition was changed to 'a right angle but no obtuse angle', which leaves only the two tangents. Answer -100 is a negative integer as planned. Changed: condition reworded.
key_step: Translate 'right angle attained, no obtuse angle' into tangency to the circle on AB as diameter.
justification: Diametric circle, the inside/outside angle fact and the tangency distance: a routine three-step chain once decoded; numerical answer. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q2 (L2).
